newsitem.title: USA: HEALTHSOUTH to continue to expand network.
newsitem.headline: HEALTHSOUTH to continue to expand network.

text.p: HEALTHSOUTH Corp said Monday that it would countinue to focus on growing its national network of outpatient surgical and rehabilitation facilities.

The company said its expansion is continuing into 1997 with the pending $1.6 billion acquisition of Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp and Health Images Inc, which will significantly augment diagnostic services because of the 96 percent market overlap with the company's rehabilitation and surgery facilities.

The company also said its primary focus would continue to be the implementation of its Integrated Service Model, which, at the end of 1996 was serving over 70 markets. The recent acquisition of ReadiCare Inc strengthened the Integrated Service Model as the company expanded its presence in the delivery of occupational health services.
During 1996 the company closed and integrated the acquisitions of Surgical Care Affiliates, Advantage Health Corp, Professional Sports Care Management and ReadiCare.

The company said it opened or acquired 160 new facilities in 1996, and signed over 1,100 new contracts with managed care companies and self-insured employers, bringing its total to over 2,300 contracts.

These relationships, said the company, contributed to its growth and produced significant margin improvement in 1996, when HEALTHSOUTH earned $1.49 per share on a fully-diluted basis, excluding non-recurring items, versus $1.08 in 1995.
It was the 10th straight year earnings have exceeded analysts' expectations, said the company.
HEALTHSOUTH is the nation's largest provider of outpatient surgery and rehabilitative healthcare services, with more than 1,000 locations in 50 states.
